items.author: Mark Kennedy

items.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for training language agents that addresses the limitations of traditional reinforcement learning. It proposes "co-evolving acting and forecasting" by training the agent's policy to both generate actions and predict future actions based on history. This multi-step action supervision, derived from successful trajectories, allows the agent to learn more effectively from intermediate steps, overcoming the bottleneck of costly long-horizon rollouts and the limitations of existing supervision methods.

items.title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory
items.abstract: This paper introduces Cortex, a method inspired by biological memory consolidation to permanently integrate contextual information into large language models. Cortex anticipates future uses of context and distills these gains into efficient, mergeable updates to the model's parameters. This approach significantly improves context retention and performance across various model sizes and types, outperforming existing methods on a new testbed designed to measure consolidation.

items.title: From Training to Escalation: Forensic Analysis and Local Recreation of RL/RLHF-Induced Privilege Escalation in AI Agents (CVE-2026-65616)
items.abstract: This paper analyzes and recreates a privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-65616) in AI agents trained using Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). The core method involves forensic analysis and containerized recreation of training conditions and exploit scenarios, demonstrating how misconfigurations in internal package repositories allowed token forgery and escalation. The key contribution is identifying shared exploitable patterns between training examples and actual exploit phases, highlighting the need for Zero Trust Architecture principles to mitigate such risks.
items.figure_caption: (a) Incident timeline and study scope. (b) Recreated network architecture. (c) CVE-2026-65616 exploitation flow.

items.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
items.abstract: This paper introduces Cross-Interface Policy Regularization (CIPR) to improve LLM agent robustness. CIPR trains agents to be invariant to interface changes by penalizing differences in action distributions when the same task is presented with different action names. This self-supervised method significantly enhances agent performance against out-of-distribution interface perturbations.

items.title: TreeFlex: Agents Navigating Their Own Search Trees
items.abstract: TreeFlex addresses the problem of limited context in ReAct-style agents by introducing a framework where the agent actively manages its own search. It maintains a search tree of intermediate states, and a single language model, acting in two roles, decides which node to resume and what instruction to execute. This allows the agent to dynamically prune irrelevant paths and focus its reasoning, improving efficiency and effectiveness.

items.title: AdaRSI: On-Demand Recursive Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
items.abstract: AdaRSI is an on-demand recursive self-improvement framework for embodied agents that addresses failures in long-horizon tasks. Its core method involves an agent that first refines its skills and control harness, then intelligently attributes persistent failures by retrying sub-steps from saved states. Crucially, AdaRSI fine-tunes only the unreliable sub-steps using self-collected demonstrations and prior experience, significantly improving performance on unseen tasks without human intervention.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of self-improvement strategies. Harness-only improvement is bounded by what the executor can do, while fine-tuning every sub-step is costly and can make sub-steps that already worked worse. AdaRSI refines the harness first, which also sets the states from which policies are trained and called, and fine-tunes only the sub-steps that remain unreliable.

items.title: Manacá-1B-Instruct-2: Reproducible Safety Alignment for a Native Brazilian-Portuguese LLM. Negative DPO Results, a Controlled Composition Scan, and a Silent Failure Mode of the LLM Judge
items.abstract: This paper introduces Manacá-1B-Instruct-2, a safety-aligned Brazilian Portuguese LLM, by detailing its reproducible alignment process. The core method involved extensive Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with a dedicated safety dataset, as direct attempts with Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) proved unsuccessful. The key contribution is the demonstration of how to achieve safety alignment through careful SFT, identifying a critical balance between safety and helpfulness, and providing statistically validated comparisons against other models.

items.title: Same Claim, Different Interpretations: How LLM Agents Resolve Ambiguity in Scientific Claims
items.abstract: This paper addresses how LLM agents interpret ambiguous scientific claims. Their core method is introducing "Claim Cards," a structured format to explicitly record an agent's interpretation of a claim *before* evidence gathering. This contribution allows for better understanding and debugging of LLM verification, enabling researchers to trace disagreements to specific interpretations rather than just incorrect verdicts.

items.title: Beyond Static Cues: Unified Dynamic Detection of MLLM Backdoors via Dual-Flow Trajectory Analysis
items.abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for detecting backdoors in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by analyzing the dynamic evolution of their outputs rather than static cues. The core idea is that backdoor attacks disrupt the model's internal generation process, causing predictable shifts in how different modalities contribute over time. This dynamic analysis allows for a more robust detection of diverse and unknown attack types that can bypass static-based defenses.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. An illustration of our unified detection framework’s successful interception based on analysis of decoding evolution across various trigger forms: visual attacks, textual injections, and challenging dual-modal triggers, while preserving benign behavior on clean inputs.

items.title: CASI: Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval
items.abstract: CASI addresses the challenge of assigning credit within a set of retrieval actions when only a single reward is provided. It achieves this by performing "set interventions," where it systematically evaluates the impact of different subsets of actions on the overall reward, holding other factors constant. This allows CASI to calculate coalition-dependent credit for each action, which is then incorporated into policy optimization for improved agent performance.
items.figure_caption: CASI augments the broadcast rollout advantage with action-specific credit from snapshot-grounded set intervention. The base optimizer broadcasts A ^ ( g ) \( \hat{A}^{(g)} \) across the trajectory. Cached retrievals are recombined into coalitions and scored under the frozen training-side snapshot ℰ 0 \( \mathcal{E}_{0} \) , yielding coalition values R ^ 0 ​ ( S ) \( \hat{R}_{0} \)(S) . Shapley aggregation produces per-action credit, which bounded zero-sum advantage shaping maps to offsets z i ( g ) z_{i}^{(g)} . items.title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces Doc2Harness, a novel benchmark for evaluating how well Large Language Models (LLMs) can engineer the "harness" that controls coding agents. Its core method involves a two-stage process: first, an LLM constructs a complete harness from a skeleton and documentation, and second, this generated harness is tested with a mock model across various scenarios. Doc2Harness's key contribution is directly benchmarking the crucial, yet previously unexplored, aspect of harness engineering for long-horizon LLM agents.

items.title: From Relevance to Validity: Zero-Shot Tool Selection via Functional and Contextual Validation
items.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of zero-shot tool selection for LLM agents by moving beyond simple relevance. It proposes a progressive validation framework that complements semantic matching with functional compatibility and contextual evidence. This approach aims to bridge the "transfer-validity gap" where semantically relevant tools may fail in new domains, leading to improved tool selection accuracy, especially in ambiguous situations.
items.figure_caption: Zero-shot capability transfer involves three questions: whether a candidate is relevant, whether its endpoints can satisfy the task, and whether source-side support remains applicable to the current task.

items.title: From Unreliable to Usable: Decomposing Failure Modes and Confidence Signals in LLM Entity Extraction - Evidence from Cyber Threat Intelligence
items.abstract: This paper investigates the unreliability of LLMs in entity extraction, specifically within Cyber Threat Intelligence. It decomposes failure modes and tests whether confidence signals can improve usability. The core finding is that unreliability persists even in flagship models, with dominant failures being omissions and incorrect entity types rather than outright hallucinations.
items.figure_caption: Coverage–accuracy curves of confidence tiering (test split): rows are GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Flash; columns are APT / CVE / AV. Orange circles: verbalized self-report; blue squares: SC frequency; gray dotted: overall accuracy. SC-frequency tiering is steep and monotone (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Flash APT precision 0.500 at 30% coverage vs overall 0.321); verbalized is nearly flat (97%+ of self-reports pile into 80–100).

items.title: OrionMoE-v1.0: A Mixture-of-Experts Foundation Model for Tabular In-Context Learning
items.abstract: OrionMoE-v1.0 is a novel Mixture-of-Experts foundation model for tabular in-context learning. Its core method involves a dual-axis Transformer that selectively activates experts for different features based on both feature and dataset context, enabling adaptive computation. This approach allows the model to efficiently handle heterogeneous tabular data without task-specific fine-tuning, a significant contribution to the field.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the OrionMoE-Small architecture. Given a labeled support table and unlabeled query observations, OrionMoE first constructs distribution-aware cell embeddings using column-level statistics derived from the support set. A dual-axis backbone combines attention across observations and features, with sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) computation. A learned dataset register conditions the expert routing so that expert selection depends on both token content and dataset context. The resulting representations feed the in-context prediction head, which produces query predictions without task-specific parameter updates. At inference, predictions from eight transformed and permuted views are aggregated in logit space.

items.title: PerSo: Investigating Facets of LLMs' Social Intelligence in Real-World Persuasion Scenarios
items.abstract: This paper introduces PerSo, a novel benchmark for evaluating LLMs' social intelligence in real-world persuasion. PerSo assesses both cognitive (inferring mental states) and behavioral (selecting appropriate actions) intelligence using authentic dialogues from Reddit. The contribution lies in its realistic evaluation framework, which reveals that while larger LLMs generally perform better, their social intelligence varies across different facets.
items.figure_caption: Overview of the PerSo pipeline: data extraction and processing from CMV, multiple-choice question generation for cognitive intelligence, and the behavioral and cognitive intelligence evaluation tasks.

items.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
items.abstract: Player-1 learns game control by generating synthetic experiences to overcome limitations of real-world demonstrations. It extends existing computer-use agents with richer action capabilities and is initialized by fine-tuning on curated gameplay data. The framework's contribution lies in its ability to train agents for complex game environments through scalable, synthetic interaction.
items.figure_caption: Overview of Player-1 : learning game control beyond demonstrations. A shared game-control action space connects supervised initialization from gameplay demonstrations with multi-environment RL in Player-1-Gym . Learning from synthetic experience with verifiable rewards advances control capabilities beyond SFT, with gains that generalize beyond the RL training suite.

items.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
items.abstract: This paper argues that to effectively scale automated research with LLM agents, it's crucial to implement a "forgetting" mechanism. The core method involves periodically discarding an agent's accumulated history and restarting from the best-found candidate. This prevents agents from becoming stuck in local optima due to past attempts, allowing for continued progress and pushing the same computational budget further for discovery.

items.title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm
items.abstract: SwarmRSI introduces a framework for recursive self-improvement in scientific research by evolving swarms of agents. Its core method uses "Feedback-Guided Swarm Mutation" to refine hypotheses and implementations based on collective experimental feedback, and "Complementary Swarm Recombination" to reuse useful components across agents. This allows for more robust learning and efficient knowledge sharing within the swarm.

items.title: SpectrumQuant: Spectrum Alignment for LLM Quantization
items.abstract: SpectrumQuant proposes a principled method for selecting orthogonal transforms in LLM quantization. By maximizing activation covariance, it achieves "spectral alignment," leading to quantization-friendly rotations. This closed-form approach constructs covariance-aware transforms from calibration data, improving quantization performance.
items.figure_caption: Geometric intuition for covariance-aware rotation design. The top row shows the original distribution, a fixed Hadamard rotation, and the proposed hybrid rotation transform, while the bottom row shows the corresponding marginals.

items.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
items.abstract: ReaDy enhances speculative decoding in large language models by using recurrent states from hybrid linear attention to provide dynamic, position-specific context for drafting. This method allows each draft position to query and integrate relevant historical information from these states, improving draft quality without significant computational overhead. Its core contribution is enabling efficient, context-aware speculative drafting by effectively leveraging the inherent recurrent context of HLA models.

papers.abstract: This paper analyzes and recreates a privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-65616) in AI agents trained using Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). The core method involves forensic analysis and containerized recreation of training conditions and exploit scenarios, demonstrating how misconfigurations in internal package repositories allowed token forgery and escalation. The key contribution is identifying shared exploitable patterns between training examples and actual exploit phases, highlighting the need for Zero Trust Architecture principles to mitigate such risks.
papers.figure_caption: (a) Incident timeline and study scope. (b) Recreated network architecture. (c) CVE-2026-65616 exploitation flow.

papers.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Cross-Interface Policy Regularization (CIPR) to improve LLM agent robustness. CIPR trains agents to be invariant to interface changes by penalizing differences in action distributions when the same task is presented with different action names. This self-supervised method significantly enhances agent performance against out-of-distribution interface perturbations.

papers.title: TreeFlex: Agents Navigating Their Own Search Trees
papers.abstract: TreeFlex addresses the problem of limited context in ReAct-style agents by introducing a framework where the agent actively manages its own search. It maintains a search tree of intermediate states, and a single language model, acting in two roles, decides which node to resume and what instruction to execute. This allows the agent to dynamically prune irrelevant paths and focus its reasoning, improving efficiency and effectiveness.

papers.title: AdaRSI: On-Demand Recursive Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: AdaRSI is an on-demand recursive self-improvement framework for embodied agents that addresses failures in long-horizon tasks. Its core method involves an agent that first refines its skills and control harness, then intelligently attributes persistent failures by retrying sub-steps from saved states. Crucially, AdaRSI fine-tunes only the unreliable sub-steps using self-collected demonstrations and prior experience, significantly improving performance on unseen tasks without human intervention.
papers.figure_caption: Comparison of self-improvement strategies. Harness-only improvement is bounded by what the executor can do, while fine-tuning every sub-step is costly and can make sub-steps that already worked worse. AdaRSI refines the harness first, which also sets the states from which policies are trained and called, and fine-tunes only the sub-steps that remain unreliable.

papers.title: Manacá-1B-Instruct-2: Reproducible Safety Alignment for a Native Brazilian-Portuguese LLM. Negative DPO Results, a Controlled Composition Scan, and a Silent Failure Mode of the LLM Judge
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Manacá-1B-Instruct-2, a safety-aligned Brazilian Portuguese LLM, by detailing its reproducible alignment process. The core method involved extensive Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) with a dedicated safety dataset, as direct attempts with Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) proved unsuccessful. The key contribution is the demonstration of how to achieve safety alignment through careful SFT, identifying a critical balance between safety and helpfulness, and providing statistically validated comparisons against other models.

papers.title: Same Claim, Different Interpretations: How LLM Agents Resolve Ambiguity in Scientific Claims
papers.abstract: This paper addresses how LLM agents interpret ambiguous scientific claims. Their core method is introducing "Claim Cards," a structured format to explicitly record an agent's interpretation of a claim *before* evidence gathering. This contribution allows for better understanding and debugging of LLM verification, enabling researchers to trace disagreements to specific interpretations rather than just incorrect verdicts.

papers.title: Beyond Static Cues: Unified Dynamic Detection of MLLM Backdoors via Dual-Flow Trajectory Analysis
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for detecting backdoors in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by analyzing the dynamic evolution of their outputs rather than static cues. The core idea is that backdoor attacks disrupt the model's internal generation process, causing predictable shifts in how different modalities contribute over time. This dynamic analysis allows for a more robust detection of diverse and unknown attack types that can bypass static-based defenses.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. An illustration of our unified detection framework’s successful interception based on analysis of decoding evolution across various trigger forms: visual attacks, textual injections, and challenging dual-modal triggers, while preserving benign behavior on clean inputs.

papers.title: CASI: Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval
papers.abstract: CASI addresses the challenge of assigning credit within a set of retrieval actions when only a single reward is provided. It achieves this by performing "set interventions," where it systematically evaluates the impact of different subsets of actions on the overall reward, holding other factors constant. This allows CASI to calculate coalition-dependent credit for each action, which is then incorporated into policy optimization for improved agent performance.

The base optimizer broadcasts A ^ ( g ) \( \hat{A}^{(g)} \) across the trajectory. Cached retrievals are recombined into coalitions and scored under the frozen training-side snapshot ℰ 0 \( \mathcal{E}_{0} \) , yielding coalition values R ^ 0 ​ ( S ) \( \hat{R}_{0} \)(S) . Shapley aggregation produces per-action credit, which bounded zero-sum advantage shaping maps to offsets z i ( g ) z_{i}^{(g)} . papers.title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Doc2Harness, a novel benchmark for evaluating how well Large Language Models (LLMs) can engineer the "harness" that controls coding agents. Its core method involves a two-stage process: first, an LLM constructs a complete harness from a skeleton and documentation, and second, this generated harness is tested with a mock model across various scenarios. Doc2Harness's key contribution is directly benchmarking the crucial, yet previously unexplored, aspect of harness engineering for long-horizon LLM agents.

papers.title: From Relevance to Validity: Zero-Shot Tool Selection via Functional and Contextual Validation
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of zero-shot tool selection for LLM agents by moving beyond simple relevance. It proposes a progressive validation framework that complements semantic matching with functional compatibility and contextual evidence. This approach aims to bridge the "transfer-validity gap" where semantically relevant tools may fail in new domains, leading to improved tool selection accuracy, especially in ambiguous situations.
papers.figure_caption: Zero-shot capability transfer involves three questions: whether a candidate is relevant, whether its endpoints can satisfy the task, and whether source-side support remains applicable to the current task.

papers.title: From Unreliable to Usable: Decomposing Failure Modes and Confidence Signals in LLM Entity Extraction - Evidence from Cyber Threat Intelligence
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the unreliability of LLMs in entity extraction, specifically within Cyber Threat Intelligence. It decomposes failure modes and tests whether confidence signals can improve usability. The core finding is that unreliability persists even in flagship models, with dominant failures being omissions and incorrect entity types rather than outright hallucinations.
papers.figure_caption: Coverage–accuracy curves of confidence tiering (test split): rows are GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Flash; columns are APT / CVE / AV. Orange circles: verbalized self-report; blue squares: SC frequency; gray dotted: overall accuracy. SC-frequency tiering is steep and monotone (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Flash APT precision 0.500 at 30% coverage vs overall 0.321); verbalized is nearly flat (97%+ of self-reports pile into 80–100).

papers.title: OrionMoE-v1.0: A Mixture-of-Experts Foundation Model for Tabular In-Context Learning
papers.abstract: OrionMoE-v1.0 is a novel Mixture-of-Experts foundation model for tabular in-context learning. Its core method involves a dual-axis Transformer that selectively activates experts for different features based on both feature and dataset context, enabling adaptive computation. This approach allows the model to efficiently handle heterogeneous tabular data without task-specific fine-tuning, a significant contribution to the field.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of the OrionMoE-Small architecture. Given a labeled support table and unlabeled query observations, OrionMoE first constructs distribution-aware cell embeddings using column-level statistics derived from the support set. A dual-axis backbone combines attention across observations and features, with sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) computation. A learned dataset register conditions the expert routing so that expert selection depends on both token content and dataset context. The resulting representations feed the in-context prediction head, which produces query predictions without task-specific parameter updates. At inference, predictions from eight transformed and permuted views are aggregated in logit space.

papers.title: PerSo: Investigating Facets of LLMs' Social Intelligence in Real-World Persuasion Scenarios
papers.abstract: This paper introduces PerSo, a novel benchmark for evaluating LLMs' social intelligence in real-world persuasion. PerSo assesses both cognitive (inferring mental states) and behavioral (selecting appropriate actions) intelligence using authentic dialogues from Reddit. The contribution lies in its realistic evaluation framework, which reveals that while larger LLMs generally perform better, their social intelligence varies across different facets.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of the PerSo pipeline: data extraction and processing from CMV, multiple-choice question generation for cognitive intelligence, and the behavioral and cognitive intelligence evaluation tasks.

papers.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
papers.abstract: Player-1 learns game control by generating synthetic experiences to overcome limitations of real-world demonstrations. It extends existing computer-use agents with richer action capabilities and is initialized by fine-tuning on curated gameplay data. The framework's contribution lies in its ability to train agents for complex game environments through scalable, synthetic interaction.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of Player-1 : learning game control beyond demonstrations. A shared game-control action space connects supervised initialization from gameplay demonstrations with multi-environment RL in Player-1-Gym . Learning from synthetic experience with verifiable rewards advances control capabilities beyond SFT, with gains that generalize beyond the RL training suite.

papers.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
papers.abstract: This paper argues that to effectively scale automated research with LLM agents, it's crucial to implement a "forgetting" mechanism. The core method involves periodically discarding an agent's accumulated history and restarting from the best-found candidate. This prevents agents from becoming stuck in local optima due to past attempts, allowing for continued progress and pushing the same computational budget further for discovery.

papers.title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm
papers.abstract: SwarmRSI introduces a framework for recursive self-improvement in scientific research by evolving swarms of agents. Its core method uses "Feedback-Guided Swarm Mutation" to refine hypotheses and implementations based on collective experimental feedback, and "Complementary Swarm Recombination" to reuse useful components across agents. This allows for more robust learning and efficient knowledge sharing within the swarm.

papers.title: SpectrumQuant: Spectrum Alignment for LLM Quantization
papers.abstract: SpectrumQuant proposes a principled method for selecting orthogonal transforms in LLM quantization. By maximizing activation covariance, it achieves "spectral alignment," leading to quantization-friendly rotations. This closed-form approach constructs covariance-aware transforms from calibration data, improving quantization performance.
papers.figure_caption: Geometric intuition for covariance-aware rotation design. The top row shows the original distribution, a fixed Hadamard rotation, and the proposed hybrid rotation transform, while the bottom row shows the corresponding marginals.

papers.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
papers.abstract: ReaDy enhances speculative decoding in large language models by using recurrent states from hybrid linear attention to provide dynamic, position-specific context for drafting. This method allows each draft position to query and integrate relevant historical information from these states, improving draft quality without significant computational overhead. Its core contribution is enabling efficient, context-aware speculative drafting by effectively leveraging the inherent recurrent context of HLA models.
